name: new_listing_momentum_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-4
thesis: IPO listing day offers a unique trading opportunity because of extreme information asymmetry and behavioral biases. Stocks that list at a significant premium (>20% above issue price) and maintain that premium through the first 30 minutes tend to attract further momentum buying from retail FOMO, pushing prices higher. Conversely, IPOs that list at a discount or lose their listing premium within 30 minutes tend to see panic selling. The key signal is the 'listing premium persistence': if the stock holds >80% of its listing premium after 30 bars, momentum is genuine. The inefficiency exists because listing day has no historical OHLCV for the stock, making indicator-based strategies impossible. Most algo traders skip day-1 entirely, leaving the field to retail traders and IPO flippers.
universe: NSE newly listed IPOs on listing day
stock_filter: IPO size > ₹500 Cr; subscription ratio > 3x (popular IPO); BSE+NSE dual listed
session: 09:45-14:00 IST (listing day only — early close to avoid EOD confusion)

indicators.name: Premium_Persistence
indicators.params: current_premium / listing_premium where current_premium = (close - Issue_Price) / Issue_Price * 100

indicators.name: First_30_VWAP
indicators.params: VWAP computed on first 30 bars of listing

indicators.name: Volume_Profile
indicators.params: cumulative volume as % of IPO shares offered

conditions: Listing_Premium_Pct > 20 (listed at significant premium — positive sentiment)
Premium_Persistence > 0.80 after bar 30 (stock has held >80% of listing premium through initial 30 min)
close > First_30_VWAP (price above initial VWAP — not fading)
long.confirmation: Volume_Profile > 10% of shares offered (sufficient liquidity for price discovery) AND close makes new high after bar 30

conditions: Listing_Premium_Pct < 5 OR Premium_Persistence < 0.50 after bar 30 (premium fading or listed near issue price)
close < First_30_VWAP (below initial VWAP — sellers dominating)
short.confirmation: close makes new low after bar 30 AND Volume_Profile > 10%

exit.target: LONG: 60 bps from entry (IPO momentum moves tend to be large); SHORT: 40 bps from entry
exit.trailing_stop: LONG: after 40 bps, trail at 20 bps; SHORT: after 25 bps, trail at 15 bps
exit.time_stop: 90 bars (end trade well before market close on listing day)
exit.eod_rule: flatten by 14:00 IST (early — listing day can have erratic close dynamics)
exit.signal_exit: Premium_Persistence drops below 0.60 for longs (premium eroding); Bid_Ask_Imbalance flips sign

risk.position_sizing: ₹75K per trade (reduced due to extreme uncertainty on listing day; no historical vol to calibrate)

filters.vix_filter: India VIX < 22; high VIX environment makes IPO listings more volatile and unpredictable
filters.time_filter: No entry before bar 30 (09:45 IST — let initial price discovery complete); no entry after 14:00
filters.volume_filter: Volume_Profile > 10% of shares offered (minimum liquidity for meaningful price discovery)
filters.trend_filter: NIFTY 50 must not be down > 1.5% (bear market IPO listings underperform regardless of company quality)
filters.spread_filter: Bid-ask spread < 20 bps (listing day spreads are naturally very wide; 20 bps is realistic threshold)
filters.event_filter: Must be IPO listing day specifically; not applicable to re-listings or demergers
other_filters: Grey Market Premium (GMP) on listing morning was positive (informal market sentiment positive)

edge.edge_decay_risk: Low — IPO listing day dynamics are driven by retail FOMO and institutional allotment selling, both behavioral phenomena that persist; each IPO is unique making systematic replication difficult

weaknesses: IPO listing days are infrequent (20-40 material IPOs per year in India) — this is a very low-frequency strategy, unsuitable as a primary trading approach
Listing day spreads are 10-20 bps (vs normal 3-5 bps), and slippage can be 5-10 bps per side — total round-trip costs of 20-30 bps can erase much of the edge

No historical price data exists for the stock on listing day — all indicators must be computed from scratch, with no backtesting possible for the specific stock; backtesting relies on out-of-sample IPO events
prior_art: Ritter (1991) IPO underpricing; Loughran & Ritter (2004) on long-run IPO performance; Indian IPO listing day studies in NSE Working Papers; retail FOMO and flipping behavior documented in Aggarwal, Prabhala & Puri (2002)
notes: The grey market premium (GMP) available through informal dealer networks provides a strong pre-listing signal — IPOs with GMP > 30% tend to list strong. Consider tracking GMP on the morning of listing as a pre-trade filter. This strategy has the highest per-trade edge but lowest frequency of all strategies in this batch; best used as an overlay to a higher-frequency core strategy.
